key_reasoning.reason: Full removal of the assistant_project_mapping repository/service/router subsystem, replaced by a new MS_TEAMS credential_type flowing through SettingsService, settings_request_validator (new validate_ms_teams_request with singleton + feature-flag checks), codemie_tools/base/models.py CredentialTypes, and both project_settings.py and user_settings.py routers (create/update/delete paths). New abstraction (per-project singleton constraint) introduced. Bumped by the 'migrate large subsystem' red flag.

Data migration (c3d4e5f6a7b8) moves rows from assistant_project_mapping into codemie.settings with dedup/merge logic, then drops the source table; a follow-on migration (f1a2b3c4d5e6) adds a singleton unique index. Downgrade is explicitly partial/non-destructive because reconstructing dropped rows is impossible — an irreversible-once-deployed characteristic. Bumped further by the 'requires data migration' and 'changes DB schema significantly' red flags.
Diffstat reports 63 files changed across this branch (Stories 1-3 combined per the caller's note), mapping to the 16+ XXL band regardless of how many are process artifacts under docs/superpowers/.

DB-Persistence (3 alembic migrations, schema change), Service (SettingsService, settings_request_validator, AssistantService.belongs_to_project), and API (project_settings.py, user_settings.py, assistant.py, plus removal of assistant_project_mapping.py router) are all touched by a single schema-driven change. Bumped from L to XL by the 'changes database schema significantly' red flag.

The merged diff reads as a coherent, deliberate design: explicit code comments justify the non-destructive downgrade, the singleton constraint, and the feature-flag gate, with matching new tests for the migration, the validator, the repository removal, and both settings routers — little evidence of rework or unresolved ambiguity.
